data.name: VR SHOOT AROUND - Realistic basketball simulator -
data.detailed_description:
VR SHOOT AROUND is a "Simulater of basketball shoot around" that will provide you fantastic physical calculations, fantastic sounds and a fantastic rich court. Do not worry if you are not good shooter. because this simulater has "Throwing power assist" and "G.O.A.T. assist", therefore you can hit a long shot like an NBA player! Let's release your frustration!!!

About the operation status of OculusQuest (using OculusLink)



Playing with OculusQuest via OculusLink (using Oculus-cable) has been confirmed to work, but playing with OculusQuest via VirtualDesktop is not recommended by Oculus and is not supported. (But there are also reports that it works)

Game features



【 Realistic rim-net physics 】We developed a physics function to reproduce the movement of rim-net close to reality.
【 Throwing power multiplier 】You can change the magnification of the throwing power. In addition, detailed settings such as rotational force, angle, and height are also possible.
【 G.O.A.T. assist 】If set to maximum value of this function, your shot will succeed with 99.9% probability unless there is an obstacle.
【 Rim height 】You can change the height of the rim in three steps. (3.05m, 2.45m, 1.85m)
【 Court color painting 】You can change each space in the court to your favorite color.
【 Logo manager 】You can paste the selected image (PNG, JPG) from the local folder on the court.
【 Video screen 】You can play selected movie & sound file from the local folder on the screen.
【 Minigames 】You can play 3PTS CONTEST & NINE HOOPS now.

reviews.review:
I've tried about every basketball game for vr by now, so i believe i'm the right person to say that this one has the best basketball physics i've seen to date AND it has proper net physics (as opposed to what feels like prerecorded animations in other games). On the store page it doesn't state it supports the oculus rift, but in my experience it's almost fully supported PROVIDING you have a 360 setup (there's no snap turning by way of the thumbstick here). I'll compare the best (imho) basketball games, so you can choose the one that suits you best:

Physics Comparison: "Hoops VR" has also good physics but the ball feels very heavy and it's difficult to give your shot the proper curve and "Nothing but Net" also has good physics but the ball feels light, you can't achieve a proper curve here either and the way you hold the ball in it is disorienting to me (the ball appears by design a bit above your controller). In VR Shoot Around the ball [strike]is still on the light side[/strike] weight is perfect after the 21st July update and the physics are spot on (you can properly curve your shot). Unfortunately no game to date accounts for different shooting styles [strike]and those of us who rely heavily on our followthrough to guide the ball are at a disadvantage[/strike] (EDIT: See update below - after the update i consider the followthrough in VR Shoot Around almost perfect now!)

Features comparison: Hoops VR is just an arcade bball shooter. You try to make as many baskets as you can within a time limit and you can choose between a large (easy mode) and a realistic basket (hard mode). The appeal of Hoops VR is to make a name for yourself on the high score boards. It's good fun, but a bit shallow. Nothing but net on the other hand offers a full court to shoot hoops and play mini games against the AI and human opponents. It has some very unique modes like playing HORSE or a mode in which you throw the ball down the court to pass it to yourself (which is a very creative way of playing basketball in vr full court!). So if you're interested in full court and mini games go for Nothing but Net. VR Shoot Around is pretty shallow at the moment, you can just shoot in a half court and that's it. although i've read on the forums the dev is planning to add mini games as well. One notable thing about VR Shoot around is its video player though: You can load onto it a h.264 / aac video file from your pc and have it play on a tv, which you can place anywhere on the court. That's great for anybody that wants to watch a show or load his workout motivational tunes while shooting.

In conclusion i'm personally going to stick with this game as my go to bball vr experience, because of the physics. For those interested i'm gonna be posting a first look video later this day and i'll post the link here.

EDIT: Short video with my first impressions https://youtu.be/3PUkXlaEGgg

EDIT 21 July 2017: After a couple small but excellent updates, the physics are now superb! The rim stiffness and power are very realistic now and the angle was improved also - i now have to use a good followthrough for my shots to go straight. Sample 20 free throws after the 2 updates: https://youtu.be/W7J0YQDb8jc

EDIT 27 July 2017: A sample of 100 shots from all over the court. No assists enabled, which makes it kinda tough to make a shot, but will help you judge the physics: https://youtu.be/YnLpKvOeVH8
